evidence_chain: Fact: USFD reported Q1 2026 net sales of $9.6 billion, up 2.8%, with total case volume up 1.4% and independent restaurant case volume up 4.6%. Source: US Foods Q1 2026 news release and earnings-summary sources.
Fact: USFD reported Q1 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $413 million, up 6.2%. Source: US Foods Q1 2026 news release and earnings-call summary.

Fact: USFD reaffirmed fiscal 2026 guidance for adjusted EBITDA growth of 9%-13% and adjusted diluted EPS growth of 18%-24%, including the benefit of a 53rd week. Source: US Foods Q1 2026 news release.

Fact: 2025 Form 10-K summary indicates total case volume increased 1.0%, independent restaurant case volume increased 3.3%, organic independent restaurant case volume increased 2.7%, and adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of net sales improved to 4.9% from 4.6% in 2024. Source: 2025 Form 10-K summary.

Fact: Q1 2026 commentary highlighted gross profit per case improvement and ongoing self-help initiatives, including cost-of-goods and operational-efficiency work. Source: Q1 2026 earnings-call summary.

Fact: USFD Q1 2026 materials and third-party summaries referenced digital innovation, including Menu IQ, an AI-powered tool for food-cost and menu-profitability management. Source: Vending Market Watch and USFD Q1 2026 presentation summary.

Inference: Independent restaurant case growth materially above total case growth suggests USFD may be gaining share in the higher-fragmentation independent restaurant segment, but this needs verification against acquisition contribution, market traffic, and food-away-from-home inflation.

Inference: EBITDA growth above sales growth suggests productivity/self-help may be contributing, but the conclusion is not fully proven without explicit EBITDA-per-case trend, retention data, digital penetration, and fuel/labor normalization.
falsification_plan: Downgrade the distributor thesis if total case volume turns flat or negative while revenue growth remains mostly price/inflation driven.
Downgrade USFD as a reference validator if independent restaurant case growth falls below total company case growth or below relevant restaurant traffic/industry benchmarks for multiple quarters.
Downgrade if adjusted gross profit per case or EBITDA per case stagnates or declines despite revenue and case growth.
Downgrade if management stops disclosing or deemphasizes independent restaurant share gains, retention, or digital-productivity metrics.
Downgrade if Q1 2026 independent restaurant growth is later shown to be materially acquisition-driven rather than organic.
Downgrade if fuel, labor, freight, or price competition consumes the benefit of volume growth and self-help initiatives.
Downgrade if peer data from Sysco and Performance Food Group shows the same pattern purely from industry recovery, making USFD's signal non-differentiated.
Downgrade the whole restaurant-distribution funnel if CHEF, USFD, Sysco, and PFGC all show pricing-led sales growth without clear case, retention, mix, or productivity improvement.
deep_reports.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify whether USFD's independent restaurant growth reflects durable share gains from smaller distributors and procurement complexity rather than headline food-away-from-home inflation. Specific hidden signals: 1) organic independent restaurant case growth remains well above total case growth; 2) growth is volume-led, not price-led; 3) digital ordering and tools such as Menu IQ increase retention, order frequency, basket size, or salesforce productivity; 4) adjusted gross profit per case and EBITDA per case improve despite fuel, labor, and freight pressure; 5) smaller-distributor consolidation or customer wins are visible in local-market performance.
next_research_tasks: Pull USFD's latest Form 10-Q for quarter ended March 28, 2026 and extract: net sales, total case volume, organic case volume, independent restaurant case growth, gross profit, adjusted gross profit, adjusted EBITDA, cash flow, leverage, and acquisition contribution.

Read the full Q1 2026 earnings-call transcript and tag management statements on independent restaurants, customer retention, digital ordering, Menu IQ, salesforce productivity, private label, fuel/weather headwinds, and cost-of-goods savings.

Build a peer table for USFD, SYY, PFGC, and CHEF: total case growth, independent/specialty growth, inflation contribution, adjusted EBITDA growth, adjusted EBITDA margin, gross profit per case, and free cash flow conversion.
Compare USFD case growth with restaurant industry traffic, food-away-from-home CPI, and independent-restaurant health indicators to separate volume/share gains from price inflation.
Search for USFD customer-facing disclosures on digital ordering penetration, Menu IQ adoption, order frequency, retention, and private-label attach rate.
Check whether USFD's 20-quarter independent restaurant share-gain claim is supported by disclosed organic case trends and whether it remains true in the next two reported quarters.
Map local-market consolidation: identify USFD acquisitions, regional distributor exits, and any disclosed contribution from acquired volume.

Use USFD as a benchmark for CHEF: if CHEF's specialty metrics exceed USFD's broadline metrics while USFD remains healthy, upgrade the specialty-distribution subtheme; if both weaken, downgrade the overall distributor lane.
risks: Inflation illusion risk: revenue growth may come from food cost inflation and mix rather than real case volume or share gains.
Volume risk: total case volume growth of 1.4% is positive but not strong enough by itself to prove broad structural acceleration.
Segment mix risk: independent restaurant strength could be offset by weakness in chain or other customer categories.
Cost pressure risk: fuel, labor, freight, warehouse wages, and insurance can erode gross profit per case and adjusted EBITDA per case.
Competitive risk: Sysco, Performance Food Group, specialty distributors, cash-and-carry wholesalers, and local distributors can pressure pricing or service levels.
Digital adoption risk: tools such as Menu IQ may be useful but may not translate into measurable customer retention, higher order frequency, or lower cost-to-serve.
Acquisition/integration risk: acquired share gains can mask organic weakness and add integration or leverage risk.
Customer health risk: independent restaurants remain exposed to wage inflation, rent, consumer traffic softness, credit stress, and commodity volatility.
Evidence risk: some key thesis variables, including customer retention, digital penetration, and EBITDA per case, may not be disclosed consistently enough to prove the thesis.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Fact/inference: USFD operates at the broadline foodservice-distribution node of the restaurant supply chain. Map: food and non-food suppliers -> procurement/private-label sourcing -> USFD warehouses and regional distribution network -> digital ordering, salesforce, Menu IQ and operator tools -> independent restaurants, hospitality, healthcare and chain customers. Chokepoint logic: independent restaurants often lack the procurement scale, route density, working-capital flexibility, SKU breadth, and data tools of large chains, making broadline distributors a potential infrastructure bottleneck. Reference role: USFD should be compared with CHEF for specialty distribution, Sysco for broadline scale, Performance Food Group for distribution consolidation, and restaurant-chain traffic data for true demand.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 推论：USFD 是餐厅主题中的参考型公司，而不是最强 underfollowed 标的。它处在美国餐饮采购基础设施的广域配送层，连接独立餐厅、医疗、酒店等客户与上游食品、饮料、非食品用品和私有品牌供应。若 USFD 能持续披露独立餐厅 case 增长、总 case 增长高于行业客流、数字订货和菜单利润工具提升客户黏性、毛利/每箱 EBITDA 改善，则说明餐饮分销链条可能存在结构性份额机会，而不只是食品通胀或餐饮需求恢复。当前 Q1 2026 证据偏正面：总 case volume 增长 1.4%，独立餐厅 volume 增长 4.6%，调整后 EBITDA 增长 6.2% 至 4.13 亿美元，且公司重申 2026 年调整后 EBITDA 增长 9%-13% 的指引。但该判断仍需用客户留存、数字渗透率、每箱利润、燃油/劳动力成本和同行对比继续验证。
deep_reports.thesis_en: Inference: USFD is a reference company within the Restaurants theme, not the strongest underfollowed candidate. It sits in the broadline foodservice distribution layer, linking independent restaurants, healthcare, hospitality, and other operators with food, beverage, non-food, and private-label supply. If USFD continues to show independent-restaurant case growth, total case growth above industry traffic, digital-ordering/menu-profitability tools that improve retention, and gross-profit or EBITDA-per-case gains, it supports the view that restaurant procurement infrastructure is gaining structural share rather than merely passing through food inflation or benefiting from broad restaurant recovery. Current Q1 2026 evidence is positive: total case volume rose 1.4%, independent restaurant volume rose 4.6%, adjusted EBITDA rose 6.2% to $413 million, and the company reaffirmed 2026 adjusted EBITDA growth guidance of 9%-13%. The thesis still requires further validation through customer retention, digital penetration, per-case profitability, fuel/labor cost pressure, and peer comparison.

deep_reports.why_underfollowed: USFD is not truly underfollowed; it is a large-cap reference company with meaningful institutional coverage. However, restaurant-theme investors may underweight it because it is less consumer-facing than restaurant chains and does not have the same brand-level same-store-sales narrative. The possibly missed signal is not restaurant traffic itself but distributor-level case growth, independent customer retention, private-label mix, digital order penetration, gross profit per case, and route/productivity gains.

summary: USFD is a reference-lane deep-research target for the Restaurants theme, not the main underfollowed alpha candidate. Its role is to validate whether the restaurant procurement infrastructure thesis is supported by real case-volume gains, independent restaurant share gains, digital ordering/productivity, and EBITDA-per-case improvement rather than merely food inflation. Current evidence supports a constructive reference signal: Q1 2026 net sales grew 2.8%, total case volume grew 1.4%, independent restaurant volume grew 4.6%, adjusted EBITDA grew 6.2% to $413 million, and management reaffirmed 2026 adjusted EBITDA growth guidance of 9%-13%. The thesis should still be tested against inflation contribution, fuel/labor headwinds, chain-volume weakness, customer-retention evidence, and whether digital tools such as Menu IQ translate into measurable retention, order frequency, or cost-to-serve improvements.
